pattern: \bnot (to be used|intended( to be used?)?) for ([\w-]+ ){0,2}(navigation|planning)\b
why: The Pacific Northwest Trail line's "not intended for trip planning": decision 38 rules that a condition a hiker's planning tool cannot meet holds its layer, so no answer row exists for it. This phrase reads that class as "not to be used" or "not intended (to be used)" for navigation or planning, with up to two words between: BMECC's "not intended for navigation purposes", CFPA's "not intended to be use for navigation" (its typo, which the phrase missed until then) and Indiana DNR's "NOT INTENDED TO BE USED FOR ON-THE-GROUND NAVIGATION". A bar on derived works: tiling and simplifying are derived works, and no decision names it
A Creative Commons non-commercial licence: decision 36 answered layers that bar profit in their own words, not this licence's terms, which a person reads before anything publishes under it

The phrase cuts the disclaimer's own words and leaves what follows them to be read, where until 2026-10-15 it ran on to the next full stop and took a ban in the same sentence with it ("should not be considered authoritative and may not be redistributed", review findings S2-1 and F1)
